questions.q: What does this course teach that earlier courses' manual Portal provisioning didn't?
options: How to click through the Azure Portal faster
A replacement for understanding what any Azure resource does
Describing the same resources (Storage Accounts, Fabric Capacities, Event Hubs) in a text file, checked into Git, applied the same way every time
What a Storage Account or Fabric Capacity is, from scratch
questions.explain: This course assumes you already know these resources from earlier courses — it teaches provisioning them as code, not what they are.

questions.q: Why is manual Portal provisioning hard to review, compared to infrastructure as code?
options: There's no diff or history for a sequence of clicks, unlike a pull request against a text file
Code review tools don't work on any kind of file
Manual provisioning is actually easier to review than code
The Azure Portal doesn't allow any resources to be created manually
questions.explain: A PR reviews infrastructure code the same way it reviews application code — there's no equivalent diff for a sequence of Portal clicks.

questions.q: What's the key difference between an imperative Azure CLI script and a declarative IaC file?
options: The script is a list of steps to run once; the IaC file describes the end state, and running it again with no changes does nothing
Imperative scripts are always faster to write
There is no real difference between the two approaches
Declarative tools cannot create real Azure resources
questions.explain: That "running it again does nothing" property is called idempotency — the defining trait of declarative IaC.

questions.q: What does "drift" mean in the context of infrastructure as code?
options: When a cloud region becomes unavailable
When a Terraform file fails to parse
When two engineers write the same resource block
When real infrastructure no longer matches what the code says it should be
questions.explain: Drift happens when someone changes a resource outside the IaC workflow — e.g. editing a setting directly in the Portal.

questions.q: Why did this track's own capstone projects (Project 2's migration, Project 3's fraud detector) actually need IaC, per this lesson?
options: They needed a full set of Azure resources provisioned in a way that's reviewable, repeatable across environments, and recoverable if something is deleted
The capstone projects only ran on resources that already existed with no provisioning
IaC was not actually relevant to either capstone project
IaC replaced the need for any pipeline code in those projects
questions.explain: Provisioning real infrastructure before a pipeline can run is exactly the gap manual, one-off Portal clicking can't reliably fill at that scale.
